THIS CRIMINAL MISC. CASE HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 11.12.2024, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 2024:KER:93804 CRL.MC NO. 7273 OF 2024 3  ORDER Petitioners are the accused in Crime No.22 of 2018 registered at the Melattur Police Station alleging commission of offences punishable under Sections 420, 406 r/w 34 of the Indian Penal Code, now pending as C.C No.282 of 2018 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court - II,
Perinthalmanna.

entities.text:
Judicial First Class Magistrate Court - II,
Perinthalmanna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The de facto complainant/3rd respondent is the mother of the 1st petitioner and the 2nd petitioner is his wife.
The crime is registered on the 3rd respondent's complaint that she was duped into registering a settlement deed in favour of the petitioners and later, thrown out of her house.

3. Learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that the dispute, which gave rise to the complaint and registration of the crime, is settled and Annexure B affidavit have been filed by the 3rd respondent vouching this fact.
4. Learned Counsel for the 3rd respondent also submitted that the dispute is settled and his client has no grievance against the petitioners.
5. I heard the learned Government Pleader also.

6. Having considered the gravity of the offences alleged and having perused the affidavit, the contents of which are vouched to be true and voluntary by the Counsel for the 3rd respondent, I am satisfied that no public interest is involved in this matter and the dispute has been settled amicably.
In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties, there is no possibility of the criminal proceedings ending in conviction.

As such, continuance of the proceedings will amount to an abuse of process of court and hence, in view of the legal position set out by the Honourable Supreme Court Vinod vs State Of Kerala on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29622131/
2
